findings: Left ventricular hypertrophy from chronic hypertension

echoTasks.find: Flap beyond the left subclavian with true and false lumens and delayed false lumen flow
Normal ascending aorta without flap, confirming confinement beyond the arch
Entry tear localisation with colour flow in both lumens on transoesophageal imaging

exam.general: Distressed with back pain between the shoulder blades, haemodynamically stable
exam.other: All peripheral pulses felt, no deficit, urine output maintained

history.a: Sudden severe back pain between the shoulder blades this morning while straining
Known hypertensive for 12 years on two drugs, missed doses this week
No chest pain, no breathlessness, no leg weakness
No prior chest surgery, no major trauma
history.q: Prior chest surgery or major trauma

history.a: Clerk, smoker, pain 9 of 10 at onset now 5 of 10
Wife present, understands need for ICU care

keyPoints: Admit to intensive care with continuous pressure monitoring and a target systolic below 120 mmHg per the aortic guideline
Start intravenous beta blockade first for rate and shear control, adding vasodilators only after
Confirm anatomy with CT aortography and classify as uncomplicated only when no malperfusion, expansion or refractory pain exists
Watch for complicated features hourly with pain scores, lactate, urine output and limb checks
Plan lifelong surveillance imaging with smoking cessation and strict pressure control
management.model: ICU medical management with shear control, CT confirmation, hourly complication watch, and lifelong surveillance

accept: type B, beyond the left subclavian
required.answer: type B, beyond the left subclavian

stem: A 55 year old hypertensive clerk from Bhopal develops sudden severe back pain between the shoulder blades while straining. Pulses are equal with no pulse deficit and no new murmur.
teaching: Pain confined to the back with a normal ascending aorta points beyond the arch
Uncomplicated type B means no malperfusion, expansion or refractory pain, and it is managed medically
Shear control starts with rate control, never a pure vasodilator first
Hourly limb, urine and lactate checks catch conversion to complicated disease
title: Uncomplicated Stanford type B aortic dissection
